correctness.rationale: Probability normalization and orthonormality of the classical second-kind Chebyshev system were checked directly. BV derivative-measure representation and Minkowski reduce the sharp Hilbert-space norm to a unit step with interior attainment. Explicit coefficient integration, Parseval, and the positive tail agree. The all-degree local midpoint curvature follows by a telescoping rational identity. A uniform large-degree summand expansion, oscillatory-tail Abel summation, endpoint exclusion, and matching phase-aligned near-midpoint jumps establish the sharp two-term squared-norm expansion. Exact finite curvature arithmetic and independent numerical tail comparisons passed after executing the attached standalone checker; the numerical checks are not proofs of the limiting optimization.

originality.rationale: The new claim controls the entire high-degree second-kind Chebyshev orthogonal projection residual in the normalized semicircle L2 space, including its sharp second-order parity-dependent midpoint deficit and its all-degree curvature sign. Closely related accessible primary papers either consider collocation, interpolation, coefficientwise sharpness, or different approximation norms. Neither existing first-kind Chebyshev nor Legendre BV residual norms imply this second-kind result through a change of parameter because their orthogonality measures and projection kernels differ. Historical unindexed equivalence remains possible.

value.rationale: For a canonical normalized Jacobi weight, the theorem gives a sharp joint-coefficient approximation benchmark with the first nontrivial correction, not merely a standard O(n^-1/2) rate. Its exact parity-curvature identity shows a real structural incompatibility: the midpoint is asymptotically globally optimal in position, but a strict local minimum for every odd cutoff. A phase-adjusted off-center jump quantifies the exact second-order penalty, motivating the particular norm and coefficient instead of an arbitrary finite calculation.
